ann_30.text: This part acts on 157 of 242 training patients (65%), and 95 of them had heart disease.

For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with 1 vessel coloured, a flat ST segment, 1.0 mm of ST depression and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG), it raises the predicted risk from about 99% to above 99%.
Through it, each extra vessel coloured adds about the same: going from 0 to 2 vessels raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 25%.
A flat ST segment raises it through this part from about 9% to about 14%.

ann_31.text: Through this part, non-anginal chest pain lowers a typical patient's predicted risk of heart disease from about 9% to about 2%.
It compares non-anginal chest pain with all other chest pain types taken together.

ann_32.text: This part acts on 49 of 242 training patients (20%), all of them patients with a normal resting ECG; 31 of them had heart disease.
For the typical patient it acts on (a 57-year-old man with a normal resting ECG, 1.6 mm of ST depression, a flat ST segment and a reversible thallium defect), the predicted risk stays at about 99%.

Through it, more ST depression on exercise adds nothing until about 1 mm, where this part switches on for patients with a normal resting ECG, then raises the predicted risk steadily: for a typical patient from about 9% at 0 mm to about 33% at 2.8 mm.

For the typical patient with this bend (a 54-year-old man with a normal resting ECG and 0.4 mm of ST depression), the same pattern, nothing until about 1 mm and then steadily, takes the predicted risk from about 5% at 0 mm to about 36% at 3.5 mm.

Across the whole model, more ST depression raises the predicted risk more if the resting ECG is normal (from about 5% to about 69%, against about 5% to about 31% otherwise); with a normal resting ECG it rises slowly at first, then faster.
On its own through this part, the resting ECG barely moves the predicted risk of the typical patient it acts on, which stays at about 99%.

ann_33.text: Through this part, each extra vessel coloured adds about the same: going from 0 to 2 vessels raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 54%.
A higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way across patients through this part, from about 10% at 118 to about 8% at 175 beats per minute.

ann_34.text: For a typical patient, the model gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease with typical angina (below 1%), non-anginal chest pain (below 1%) or atypical angina (about 2%) than with no chest pain symptoms (about 9%).

Each extra vessel coloured adds about the same: going from 0 to 2 vessels raises a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% to about 99%, flattening out near the top because it cannot go much higher.
A flat ST segment raises it to about 87%, a reversible defect or the undefined code 4 on the thallium scan to about 44%, and chest pain brought on by exercise to about 16%.
More ST depression on exercise raises it in an uneven way across patients, for a typical patient from about 5% at 0 mm to about 69% at 2.8 mm.

Higher cholesterol and higher resting blood pressure each raise it steadily: from about 3% at 193 mg/dL to about 28% at 308 mg/dL, and from about 4% at 110 mm Hg to about 20% at 155 mm Hg, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower.
Being a woman lowers it from about 9% to below 1%, and a fixed defect on the thallium scan to about 1% (the model has little data on this, n = 15).
Fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it to about 4%, and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way across patients, from about 10% at 118 to about 8% at 175 beats per minute.

sentences.text: These add up independently: compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina and non-anginal chest pain lower the predicted risk from about 9% to below 1%, and atypical angina to about 2%; being a woman lowers it to below 1%, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 4%.

A reversible defect or the undefined code 4 on the thallium scan raises it to about 44%, and chest pain brought on by exercise to about 16%; higher cholesterol (from about 3% at 193 mg/dL to about 28% at 308 mg/dL) and higher resting blood pressure (from about 4% at 110 mm Hg to about 20% at 155 mm Hg) raise it steadily, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower.

The number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy, the slope of the ST segment and ST depression on exercise also enter this sum, and act through the parts below as well: across the whole model, each extra vessel adds about the same (from about 9% at 0 to about 99% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher), a flat ST segment raises it to about 87%, and more ST depression raises it in an uneven way, from about 5% at 0 mm to about 69% at 2.8 mm.
A fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the risk to about 1% (the model has little data on this, n = 15).

This part combines the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy with the maximum heart rate: through it, each extra vessel adds about the same, raising a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% at 0 to about 54% at 2 vessels.
A higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way, from about 10% at 118 to about 8% at 175 beats per minute, through this part as across the whole model.
This part combines the number of vessels coloured with a flat ST segment, and acts on 157 of 242 training patients, 95 of whom had heart disease.
Through it, each extra vessel adds about the same, from about 9% at 0 to about 25% at 2 vessels for a typical patient, and a flat ST segment raises the risk from about 9% to about 14%.
This part combines the resting ECG with ST depression on exercise, and acts on 49 of 242 training patients, all of them with a normal resting ECG; 31 of them had heart disease.

Through it, more ST depression adds nothing until about 1 mm, where this part switches on for patients with a normal resting ECG, then raises the predicted risk steadily: for a typical patient from about 9% at 0 mm to about 33% at 2.8 mm.

Across the whole model, ST depression therefore counts more with a normal resting ECG: going from 0 to 2.8 mm moves a typical patient from about 5% to about 69%, rising slowly at first, then faster, but only from about 5% to about 31% otherwise.

ann_30.original: Hidden node 664 = ReLU(0.601*ca + 0.326*slope:2 + 0.664), read out with +0.983. Hypothesis (supported): a near-affine risk term in number of major vessels coloured (ca) and flat ST slope (slope:2). On train the pre-activation ranges [-0.071, 2.607]; the ReLU clips only the 85 rows with ca at its minimum and slope:2=0, and only by <=0.071 (<=0.07 logit). Replacing the ReLU by identity leaves train AUC unchanged (0.9392 -> 0.9390); mean-ablating the node costs 0.002 AUC. Contribution SD 0.70 logit. So this is effectively +0.59*ca + 0.32*slope:2 added to the logit, on top of the direct ca and slope:2 edges.
ann_30.proposed: A part that acts on about two thirds of patients; through it, more vessels coloured and a flat ST segment raise the predicted risk.

ann_31.original: Hidden node 1173 = ReLU(0.505*cp:3 + 1.92) is active on 100% of train rows (pre-activation in [1.59, 2.71]), so it is an affine relay: with readout -1.305 it contributes -0.658*cp:3 - 2.50 to the logit. Supported: line plot entry/exit correlation 1.0; removing the ReLU changes no prediction (AUC 0.9392 unchanged); mean-ablation costs 0.004 AUC. Meaning: non-anginal chest pain (cp:3) lowers predicted disease risk. cp:3 has no direct edge, so this is its only route to the output.
ann_31.proposed: Non-anginal chest pain lowers the predicted risk through this part.

ann_32.original: Hidden node 1801 = ReLU(1.48*restecg:0 + 0.805*oldpeak - 1.43), readout +1.335. Hypothesis (supported): an interaction gate, the network's only consequential nonlinearity. restecg:0 takes values +/-1 (121 rows each on train). With restecg:0=+1 the gate passes ReLU(0.805*oldpeak + 0.05), active on 39.7% of those rows (exercise ST depression above about its median); with restecg:0=-1 it is active on 1/121 rows (needs oldpeak > 3.6 SD). So ST depression adds up to ~+3.4 extra logit, but only when restecg:0=+1. The ReLU matters: replacing it by identity drops train AUC 0.9392 -> 0.9162 (the linear version would add a large restecg:0 main effect); mean-ablating the whole node costs only 0.0001 AUC, so its value is the shape, not the extra ranking signal over the direct oldpeak edge (+0.869). Overall active rate 20%, contribution SD 0.55 logit.
ann_32.proposed: A part that acts on patients with a normal resting ECG; through it, ST depression above about 1.0 mm raises the predicted risk, so ST depression matters more with a normal resting ECG.

ann_33.original: Serial chain ca -> 2245 -> 2009 <- thalach. 2245 = ReLU(0.781*ca + 1.25) is always active on train (pre in [0.68, 3.31]); its readout +1.669 adds +1.30*ca + 2.08 to the logit (SD 1.30, the largest hidden contribution; mean-ablation costs 0.007 AUC). 2009 = ReLU(0.949*thalach + 1.36*2245 + 0.179) = ReLU(0.949*thalach + 1.06*ca + 1.87) is active on 93.8% of rows (clipped for 15 rows with very low max heart rate and few vessels); readout -0.165 gives a small -0.157*thalach - 0.175*ca term (SD 0.20). Hypothesis (supported): mostly affine; ca raises risk, higher max heart rate slightly lowers it; the 2009 ReLU is near-inert (removing it: AUC 0.9392 -> 0.9391).
ann_33.proposed: More vessels coloured raise the predicted risk through this part; a higher maximum heart rate lowers it, from about 10% at 118 to about 8% at 175 beats per minute for a typical patient.

ann_34.original: Root: output node 0 computes the logit z = -0.160 + LINEAR CORE + hidden readouts, and (binary task) the model applies a sigmoid at the output (get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU; decision is z>0). LINEAR CORE: 15 direct edges, largest |w|: sex:0 -2.01 (female lowers risk), slope:2 +1.85, ca +1.53, cp:4 (asymptomatic) +1.32, thal:3 (normal) -1.04, chol +1.01, thal:6 -0.97, cp:1 -0.93, oldpeak +0.87, trestbps +0.72; SD 5.29 of a 7.04 total logit SD. Children add: +0.983*ca_slope2_gate (near-affine in ca, slope:2), -1.305*cp3_affine_relay (affine, -0.66 cp:3), +1.669*2245 and -0.165*2009 from ca_thalach_chain (mostly affine: +1.30 ca, small -thalach), and +1.335*normal_ecg_st_gate (the one real interaction: oldpeak adds extra risk only when restecg:0=+1). Composition is purely additive at node 0. Hypothesis (supported): the network is a logistic regression in which ca appears through three parallel affine routes (total ~+3.4 per SD), plus one gated ST-depression term. Evidence (train, n=242): AUC 0.939, acc 0.888. Replacing every ReLU by identity gives AUC 0.916, almost exactly the loss from removing only the 1801 ReLU (0.916), so 1801 is the only nonlinearity that matters; the other ReLUs change AUC by <=0.0002. Inputs age, sex:1, fbs:0, restecg:2, exang:1, slope:1, slope:3, thal:4, thal:7 are unconnected.
ann_34.proposed: Typical angina, non-anginal chest pain and atypical angina lower the predicted risk compared with no chest pain symptoms. More vessels coloured, a flat ST segment, more ST depression, a reversible thallium defect, higher cholesterol, higher resting blood pressure and chest pain on exercise raise it; being a woman lowers it. The model ignores age.

lead.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results) the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about 9%; most of its inputs add up independently, and three parts change that sum: two add more for each extra vessel coloured, and one acts only on the 49 of 242 training patients with a normal resting ECG.

summary.text: For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results) the model predicts a risk of heart disease of about 9%; most of its inputs add up independently, and three parts change that sum: two add more for each extra vessel coloured, and one acts only on the 49 of 242 training patients with a normal resting ECG.

These add up independently: compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina and non-anginal chest pain lower the predicted risk from about 9% to below 1%, and atypical angina to about 2%; being a woman lowers it to below 1%, and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 4%.

A reversible defect or the undefined code 4 on the thallium scan raises it to about 44%, and chest pain brought on by exercise to about 16%; higher cholesterol (from about 3% at 193 mg/dL to about 28% at 308 mg/dL) and higher resting blood pressure (from about 4% at 110 mm Hg to about 20% at 155 mm Hg) raise it steadily, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower.

The number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy, the slope of the ST segment and ST depression on exercise also enter this sum, and act through the parts below as well: across the whole model, each extra vessel adds about the same (from about 9% at 0 to about 99% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher), a flat ST segment raises it to about 87%, and more ST depression raises it in an uneven way, from about 5% at 0 mm to about 69% at 2.8 mm.
A fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers the risk to about 1% (the model has little data on this, n = 15).

This part combines the number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy with the maximum heart rate: through it, each extra vessel adds about the same, raising a typical patient's predicted risk from about 9% at 0 to about 54% at 2 vessels.
A higher maximum heart rate lowers it in an uneven way, from about 10% at 118 to about 8% at 175 beats per minute, through this part as across the whole model.

This part combines the resting ECG with ST depression on exercise, and acts on 49 of 242 training patients, all of them with a normal resting ECG; 31 of them had heart disease.

Through it, more ST depression adds nothing until about 1 mm, where this part switches on for patients with a normal resting ECG, then raises the predicted risk steadily: for a typical patient from about 9% at 0 mm to about 33% at 2.8 mm.

Across the whole model, ST depression therefore counts more with a normal resting ECG: going from 0 to 2.8 mm moves a typical patient from about 5% to about 69%, rising slowly at first, then faster, but only from about 5% to about 31% otherwise.

ann_30.text: This part acts on 157 of 242 training patients (65%).
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 99% without this part to above 99% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 95 of these 157 patients had heart disease.

Through this part, the model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 9% at 0 vessels to about 25% at 2 vessels (on the training data only).

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 14%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 9%) (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient has non-anginal chest pain (about 2%) than if chest pain type is something other than non-anginal chest pain (about 9%) (on the training data only).

ann_32.text: This part acts on 49 of 242 training patients (20%); nearly all of them are patients with a normal resting ECG.
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly raises the predicted risk of heart disease from about 99% without this part to about 99% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 31 of these 49 patients had heart disease.

A higher ST depression on exercise clearly raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal (slowly at first, then faster for patients with a normal resting ECG): for a typical patient, ST depression on exercise going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 5% to about 69% if the resting ECG is normal, and from about 5% to about 31% if resting ECG is something other than a normal resting ECG.

Other effects: ST depression on exercise past about 1.0 mm raises it with nothing until about 1.0 mm, then steadily; a higher ST depression on exercise raises it with nothing until about 1.0 mm, then steadily (on the training data only).
Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: any other resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG) lowers it (on the training data only).

ann_33.text: Through this part, the model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 9% at 0 vessels to about 54% at 2 vessels (on the training data only).

Through this part, the model treats a higher maximum heart rate as slightly lowering the predicted risk of heart disease in an uneven way: for a typical patient, it goes from about 10% at 118 beats per minute to about 8% at 175 beats per minute (on the training data only).

ann_34.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 9% at 0 vessels to about 99% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 87%) than if slope of the ST segment at peak exercise is something other than a flat ST segment (about 9%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease in an uneven way: for a typical patient, it goes from about 5% at 0.0 mm to about 69% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if thallium stress test result is something other than a normal thallium scan, a fixed defect on the thallium scan (about 44%) than if the thallium scan is normal (about 9%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher serum cholesterol as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 3% at 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to about 28% at 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L), flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower (on the training data only).

Other effects: a higher resting blood pressure raises it steadily; typical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; female (rather than male) lowers it; non-anginal chest pain (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it; chest pain brought on by exercise (rather than no chest pain on exercise) raises it; a fixed defect on the thallium scan (rather than a normal thallium scan) lowers it; atypical angina (rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic)) lowers it (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).
